subject: maths
title: Chapter 8 · Test 1
summary: Chapter 8 test 1: expanding binomials, special products, factorising and algebraic fractions — 15 questions.
body:
This is Chapter 8 · Test 1. It covers all of Chapter 8, Algebraic techniques: expanding binomial products, perfect squares and difference of two squares, factorising by common factors, factorising quadratic trinomials and simplifying algebraic fractions.

There are 15 questions: 4 easy, 5 medium, 4 hard and 2 challenge. Allow about 25 minutes. Work with no notes and no calculator unless the question says. Show your working on paper, and check each answer by expanding or by substituting a simple number such as x = 2.

questions.explanation: The four products are x², 9x, 2x and 18, so x² + 11x + 18. x² + 18 leaves out the two middle products.
steps: Products: x × x = x², x × 9 = 9x, 2 × x = 2x, 2 × 9 = 18.

mistakes.B: Step 1: there are four products — include 9x and 2x.
mistakes.C: Step 1: the last term is 2 × 9, not 2 + 9.
mistakes.D: Step 2: the middle term is 9x + 2x, not 2 × 9 lots of x.

questions.prompt: The rectangle in the diagram has width x + 7 and height x + 1. Which expression is its area, fully expanded?
questions.explanation: The four boxes are x², 7x, x and 7, so the area is x² + 8x + 7. x² + 7x + 7 misses the box under x, which is x × 1.
steps: Fill the boxes: x × x = x², 7 × x = 7x, x × 1 = x, 7 × 1 = 7.

mistakes.A: Step 1: the two strips 7x and x are part of the area too.
mistakes.B: Step 1: area multiplies the sides; you added them.
mistakes.D: Step 1: you missed the box x × 1 = x.

questions.diagram_alt: A rectangle with x and 7 along the top and x and 1 down the side, split into four empty boxes

questions.explanation: The HCF of 9 and 12 is 3; 9x ÷ 3 = 3x and 12 ÷ 3 = 4, giving 3(3x + 4). 3(3x + 12) forgets to divide the 12.
steps: Divide each term by 3: 3x and 4, so 3(3x + 4).

mistakes.A: Step 2: divide every term by 3, including the 12.
mistakes.D: Step 1: 12 has no x, so x is not a common factor.

questions.topic: Perfect squares and difference of two squares
questions.explanation: Same terms, opposite signs: difference of two squares, x² − 10² = x² − 100. x² + 100 misses that 10 × −10 is negative.
steps: Use (a + b)(a − b) = a² − b² with a = x and b = 10.

mistakes.C: Step 1: that is (x − 10)²; here the middle terms cancel.

questions.explanation: 2 × 7 = 14 and 2 + 7 = 9, so (x + 2)(x + 7). (x + 1)(x + 14) multiplies to 14 but adds to 15.
steps: The pair adding to 9 is 2 and 7, so (x + 2)(x + 7).

mistakes.D: Step 1: 3 × 6 = 18, not 14 — check the product as well as the sum.

questions.topic: Perfect squares and difference of two squares
questions.explanation: Square, double, square: x², 2 × x × (−6) = −12x, (−6)² = 36. x² − 12x − 36 forgets that a negative squared is positive.
steps: Square the first: x². Double the product: 2 × x × (−6) = −12x.

mistakes.A: Step 1: (x − 6)² = (x − 6)(x − 6), which has a middle term.
mistakes.D: Step 1: double the product — there are two −6x terms.

questions.explanation: Products: 3x², −12x, 2x and −8; −12x + 2x = −10x, so 3x² − 10x − 8. 3x² − 14x − 8 treats the inner product as −2x.

mistakes.A: Step 3: the inner product is +2x, so add it to −12x.
mistakes.D: Step 2: don't forget the inner product 2 × x.

questions.explanation: The HCF is 3a, so 6a² + 15a = 3a(2a + 5). 3(2a² + 5a) is equal but not fully factorised (the bracket still shares a).
steps: HCF: 3 (from 6 and 15) and a (in both terms), so 3a.

mistakes.A: Step 1: both terms also contain a — take it out too.
mistakes.B: Step 1: 6 and 15 also share a 3 — take it out too.

questions.explanation: 20 ÷ 4 = 5 and x³ ÷ x = x², so 5x². 5x³ forgets to cancel the x on the bottom.
steps: Cancel the letters: x³ ÷ x = x², so 5x².

mistakes.B: Step 2: the x on the bottom cancels one of the three x's on top.
mistakes.D: Step 2: x³ ÷ x = x²; only one x cancels.

questions.explanation: −7 × 3 = −21 and −7 + 3 = −4, so (x − 7)(x + 3). (x + 7)(x − 3) gives a middle term of +4x.
steps: c is negative, so the signs differ; b = −4, so the bigger number is negative.
Pairs for −21: −7 and 3 add to −4, so (x − 7)(x + 3).

mistakes.A: Step 2: 7 + (−3) = +4 — the bigger number must be negative.

questions.explanation: x² − 36 = (x + 6)(x − 6), and the (x + 6) cancels, leaving x − 6. x + 6 cancels the wrong bracket.
steps: Cancel (x + 6) top and bottom, leaving x − 6.

mistakes.A: Step 2: (x + 6) is the bracket that cancels; keep the other one.
mistakes.C: Step 1: factorise first — you can't cancel 36 with 6 through a minus sign.
mistakes.D: Step 2: the bracket that is left is on the TOP.

questions.explanation: Both parts contain (a + 3); taking it out leaves 4 − a, so (a + 3)(4 − a). (a + 3)(4 + a) drops the minus sign in front of a.
steps: The common factor is the bracket (a + 3).
What is left is 4 from the first part and −a from the second, so (a + 3)(4 − a).

mistakes.A: Step 2: the a has a minus sign in front of it, which goes into the bracket.
mistakes.B: Step 2: the 4 is positive and the a is negative, not the other way round.
mistakes.C: Step 1: that is the expanded form; the question asks you to factorise.

questions.explanation: (x + 6)(x − 1) = x² + 5x − 6 and −2x(x + 2) = −2x² − 4x. Together: −x² + x − 6. −x² + 9x − 6 treats −2x × 2 as +4x.
steps: Expand the second part with its minus: −2x(x + 2) = −2x² − 4x.

mistakes.C: Step 2: the second part is subtracted, so it is −2x², not +2x².

questions.explanation: Top: (x − 5)(x + 2). Bottom: (x + 5)(x − 5). Cancel (x − 5) to get (x + 2)/(x + 5). (x − 2)/(x − 5) comes from factorising the top as (x + 5)(x − 2).

mistakes.A: Step 1: (x + 5)(x − 2) expands to x² + 3x − 10 — check the middle sign.
mistakes.C: Step 3: the bracket that cancels is (x − 5), so (x + 5) stays on the bottom.
mistakes.D: Step 1: x² is a term, not a factor — factorise before cancelling.

questions.topic: Perfect squares and difference of two squares
questions.prompt: Use a perfect square to work out 99² without a calculator.
questions.explanation: 99² = (100 − 1)² = 10 000 − 200 + 1 = 9801. 9999 squares each part and leaves out the middle term.

mistakes.B: Step 1: double the product — the middle term is 200, not 100.
mistakes.D: Step 2: the last term (−1)² = +1 must be added.
